task.title: Bring deleted text back from the history
task.description: You are in the ~/portfolio folder, and Git is configured. The history has several commits by different authors, and one of them deleted part of the text from about.html - its message starts with the word Remove. The number and hash of this commit are not known in advance: find it in the history. Write the commands one per line: 1) View the history with git log and git log --oneline. 2) Find the commit whose message starts with Remove and look at its changes (git show). 3) Print about.html from the commit BEFORE it (git show HEAD~N:about.html). 4) Write this version into about.html (the > sign) and check git status and git diff. 5) Add about.html to the index and check git diff --staged. 6) Make a commit with a message that starts with Restore (for example, Restore team section). 7) Check the history: git log --oneline -n 3.
task.starter_code:
# Write commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments.
# You are in the ~/portfolio folder, Git is configured, the history already has several commits.

# 1. Project history: detailed and short (--oneline)

# 2. Find the commit whose message starts with Remove and look at its changes

# 3. Show about.html in the commit BEFORE it (HEAD~N:about.html)

# 4. Write this version into about.html and check git status and git diff

# 5. Add the file to the index and check git diff --staged

# 6. A commit with a message that starts with Restore

# 7. Check the result in the history

tests.name: The script ran without internal errors
tests.fail: Check the quotes and the > sign in your commands.

tests.name: Exactly one new commit was added
tests.fail: You need one commit: git add about.html, then git commit -m "Restore ...". If Git answered nothing to commit, the file did not change: you took the wrong version.

tests.name: The old commits are unchanged
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.head() !== null && repo.log().slice(-6).map((c) => c.subject).join("|") === "Update README|Add link to about page|Remove team section|Add styles|Add about page|Add home page"
tests.fail: The new commit must go on top of the history; you do not need to touch the old commits.

tests.name: The Team section is back in about.html in the latest commit
tests.fail: Take about.html from the commit BEFORE the Remove team section commit: git show HEAD~3:about.html

tests.name: about.html matches the version before the deletion
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.head() !== null && repo.commit("HEAD").files["about.html"] === (() => { const r = repo.log().find((c) => c.subject.startsWith("Remove")); return r ? repo.commit(r.parents[0]).files["about.html"] : undefined; })()
tests.fail: The file must fully match the old version: git show HEAD~3:about.html > about.html (with the colon and the file name).

tests.name: The file in the working directory is restored too
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.head() !== null && sim.read("~/portfolio/about.html") === (() => { const r = repo.log().find((c) => c.subject.startsWith("Remove")); return r ? repo.commit(r.parents[0]).files["about.html"] : undefined; })()
tests.fail: Write the old version into about.html with the > sign and check cat about.html.

tests.name: The new commit changes only about.html
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.head() !== null && (() => { const a = repo.commit("HEAD").files; const b = repo.commit("HEAD~1").files; const ka = Object.keys(a).sort().join(","); const kb = Object.keys(b).sort().join(","); return ka === kb && Object.keys(b).every((f) => f === "about.html" || a[f] === b[f]) && a["about.html"] !== b["about.html"]; })()
tests.fail: Add only about.html to the index; do not change other files or create new ones.

tests.name: The commit message starts with Restore
tests.fail: Example: git commit -m "Restore team section" - in English, up to 50 characters.

tests.name: All changes are committed
tests.fail: After the commit, git status should answer nothing to commit, working tree clean.

tests.name: The history was viewed with git log
tests.fail: Start with git log and git log --oneline: this is how you find the right commit.

tests.name: The changes were viewed with git show or git diff
tests.fail: Look at what the commit deleted: git show HEAD~2.

tests.name: Different history: the deleted Skills list is restored
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.head() !== null && repo.log().length === 6 && repo.commit("HEAD").files["about.html"] === (() => { const r = repo.log().find((c) => c.subject.startsWith("Remove")); return r ? repo.commit(r.parents[0]).files["about.html"] : undefined; })() && repo.commit("HEAD").files["about.html"].includes("Skills")
tests.fail: The solution must not depend on specific text or a hash: use HEAD~N:about.html, not echo with ready-made text.

tests.name: Different history: the new Restore commit changes only about.html
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.head() !== null && /^Restore \S/.test(repo.commit("HEAD").subject) && (() => { const a = repo.commit("HEAD").files; const b = repo.commit("HEAD~1").files; const ka = Object.keys(a).sort().join(","); const kb = Object.keys(b).sort().join(","); return ka === kb && Object.keys(b).every((f) => f === "about.html" || a[f] === b[f]) && a["about.html"] !== b["about.html"]; })() && repo.status().clean
tests.fail: The hashes in the other history are different - refer to commits with HEAD~N.

hints: git log --oneline: the top line is HEAD, the next one is HEAD~1, then HEAD~2 and so on.
The Remove... commit is on the third line, so it is HEAD~2. The old text is in the commit before it: HEAD~3.
First look at the file without writing it: git show HEAD~3:about.html. If the output contains the deleted text, the version is right.
Writing to the file: git show HEAD~3:about.html > about.html - the colon and the file name are required.
Do not type the text by hand and do not use a hash: the check includes another history with different text and different hashes.
git add about.html, then git commit -m "Restore team section".

questions.question: What does git log --oneline do?
options: Shows the history: one line per commit - the short hash and the message
Deletes long messages from the history
Shows the changed lines of each commit
questions.explanation: --oneline shrinks each commit to one line: 7 characters of the hash and the first line of the message.

questions.question: Match the line from the output of git log with its meaning.
pairs: The full hash - the unique name of the commit
questions.explanation: Every commit in git log is a hash, an author, a date and a message.

questions.question: In a real terminal, git log opened a long history, and there is a colon or (END) at the bottom. How do you get back to the command line?
options: Close the terminal - there is no other way
questions.explanation: Git opens long output in a pager program (less). Space shows the next page, q (quit) exits.

questions.question: git log --oneline showed: a1b2c3d (HEAD -> main) Add footer / e4f5a6b Add styles / 9c8d7e6 Add home page. Which of these point to the Add styles commit?
questions.explanation: HEAD is Add footer, HEAD~1 and HEAD^ are its parent Add styles; e4f5a6b is the short hash of the same commit. HEAD~2 is Add home page.

questions.question: You changed index.html but have not run git add yet. What does git diff --staged show?
options: Nothing: there are no new changes in the index
questions.explanation: --staged compares the index with the latest commit. While the changes are only in the working directory, plain git diff shows them.

questions.question: Match the line of a unified diff with its meaning.
pairs: The old version of the file
The new version of the file
Where the hunk is: there were 7 lines from line 1, now there are 2 from line 1
questions.explanation: Minus means deleted, plus means added, lines without a sign are unchanged context.

questions.question: Write the command that prints the content of about.html as it was two commits ago (relative to HEAD).
questions.explanation: git show <commit>:<file> prints the file from the given commit and changes nothing in the working directory.

questions.question: How is git show HEAD~2 different from git show HEAD~2:about.html?
options: The first shows the commit (author, date, message and diff), the second shows only the content of the file in that commit
The first restores the file, the second deletes it
The second works only in Git 3.0
questions.explanation: Without a colon, git show shows the commit itself and its changes; with :file it shows a snapshot of one file.

questions.question: What is true about a commit hash?
options: It is calculated from the content of the commit, so it is different for different commits
In commands you can use the short hash - the first 7 characters
The author of the commit makes it up
In Git 2.x it is a 40-character SHA-1; in Git 3.0 the default will be a 64-character SHA-256
questions.explanation: A hash is a commit's "fingerprint": Git calculates it itself from the content, author, date and parent.

questions.question: Complete the command to see only the last 3 commits in short form: git log --oneline ___
Which command shows the difference between the two commits HEAD~3 and HEAD?
questions.explanation: git diff A B shows what must change in A to get B: lines with - were in A, lines with + appeared in B.

questions.question: You ran git show HEAD~3:about.html > about.html. What happened?
options: Git made a new commit with the old about.html
The old version of the file was written into the working directory; Git sees it as a change that still has to be added and committed
questions.explanation: The > sign writes the output into a file. The history does not change: next you need git add and git commit.
